script: Tamil script, as confirmed by the canonical MorphoVerse dataset audit (~97% of non-space characters in the sampled records)
romanization_guidance: Represent retroflex, alveolar, and dental consonant distinctions (which Tamil marks more finely than Hindi) with familiar reader-friendly digraphs rather than diacritics or subscript dots.

Tamil script does not distinguish voiced/voiceless or aspirated/unaspirated stops in writing the way the sound system may realize them in speech (e.g. a single letter can represent both a voiceless and voiced pronunciation depending on position); use the most common reader-friendly convention rather than presenting one pronunciation as definitively correct.
Use a widely-recognized conventional spelling for well-known names/places when one already exists in common English usage.
Keep every repeated occurrence of the same source term romanized identically within one poem.
linguistic_guidance: Tamil exhibits diglossia: a literary/classical register (centamil) distinct from spoken/colloquial Tamil (koduntamil); do not assume a poem is in one register without textual evidence, and do not assume literary-register vocabulary automatically signals classical-era or Sangam content.

Tamil is highly agglutinative, with case, postposition-equivalent, and verbal information fused onto word stems; a suffix's meaning collapsing into a simpler English construction is a legitimate, text-grounded translation-loss candidate.
Tamil vocabulary includes a native Dravidian core alongside Sanskrit-derived loanwords; a word's etymological origin alone does not indicate this poem's cultural specificity.
cultural_boundary_rules: A culturally specific Tamil annotation requires a defensible link to a named tradition, practice, or symbol that the poem's own text actually evidences -- do not add one merely because the poem is in Tamil.

Do not infer Sangam-era classical-literature framing, temple imagery, Bharatanatyam-dance imagery, or Dravidian-political/identity framing unless the poem's own words name or unambiguously depict that specific content -- these are common outside shorthands for 'Tamil culture' and must not be assumed as a default backdrop.
literary_context_cautions: Tamil literary history spans the classical Sangam corpus, medieval Bhakti (Shaiva/Vaishnava) devotional literature, and a substantial modern tradition (including Bharathiyar-era nationalist poetry and contemporary free verse) -- do not assume a poem belongs to a specific one without textual evidence.
translation_cautions: Watch for agglutinative case/postposition-equivalent meaning being flattened into a generic English preposition.
Watch for literary-register vocabulary being translated with an over-casual or over-formal English register that shifts the poem's tone.
figurative_language_cautions: Tamil poetic convention (from the classical akam/puram tradition onward) uses landscape and nature imagery (thinai) as conventionalized emotional signifiers; treat this as ordinary poetic convention rather than automatically a culturally specific or figurative flag unless the text gives it a specific, bounded role.
visual_representation_cautions: Do not default to temple, Bharatanatyam, or Sangam-era imagery for a Tamil cultural entity unless the text specifically supports it.
negative_confusions for an entity in this language should name a plausible, specific incorrect substitution, not a generic stereotype disconnected from the poem's own evidence.
stereotype_avoidance_rules: Do not adopt a 'this is ancient Dravidian classical literature' framing merely because the language is Tamil -- annotate only what this specific poem's text supports; most corpus poems are contemporary.
Do not apply a numeric quota (e.g. 'expect N cultural entities') to this poem -- a poem with zero text-supported cultural entities is a valid, expected outcome.
ambiguity_handling_rules: When a term's register (literary vs. colloquial) or figurative-vs-conventional status is genuinely uncertain from the text alone, prefer the more conservative reading and use the explicit-uncertainty mechanism.
When a reading is genuinely uncertain from the text alone, prefer the more conservative reading and use the explicit-uncertainty mechanism rather than asserting one interpretation as fact.
prohibited_assumptions: Do not assume classical/Sangam-era literary status, temple/religious content, or Dravidian-political framing without direct textual support.
Do not assume the speaker's religion, region, or gender beyond what the text states.
Do not assume a specific historical period unless the text itself places the poem there.
Do not assume rural versus urban setting unless the text specifies it.
